# Historical Clarabel numerical comparison

The active engine solver is now implemented directly in TypeScript in [`solveAutoMovieQuadraticKernel`](../../src/math/solveAutoMovieQuadraticKernel.ts). Conic assembly, reversible Ruiz equilibration, sparse minimum-degree ordering and LDL factorization, original-KKT iterative refinement, homogeneous predictor-corrector directions and termination are engine-owned numerical logic. It imports no external numerical solver, WebAssembly binary, native executable or solve-time service. The public interval-QP API, signed row duals, objective diagnostics and full/reduced/infeasible status distinction remain at that entry and its adapter.

The method is [Goulart and Chen (2024), sections 2-3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12762), specialized to diagonal PSD objectives and zero/nonnegative cones. Five numerical files adapt the actual Clarabel Rust processing structure and formulas; they are modified Apache-2.0 source specializations, rather than implementations derived solely from the paper. Sparse left-looking LDL uses an elimination tree and actual fill storage; the separately written exact minimum-degree ordering resolves ties by original ordinals. These arithmetic and ordering choices can change iterates and iteration counts from the historical executable. Full convergence still requires the original residual and gap criteria; no finite-precision method promises to solve every ill-conditioned input.

## TypeScript source provenance and distribution

Sparse elimination, substitutions, original-KKT refinement residuals, homogeneous scalar equations, iterate additions and original-row diagnostics use compensated product/addition sums. Their arithmetic follows [Ogita, Rump and Oishi (2005), algorithms 3.1, 3.3 and 5.3](https://www.tuhh.de/ti3/paper/rump/OgRuOi05.pdf), retaining product and addition rounding corrections in two binary64 components. This addresses cancellation between large nearly dependent multipliers while evaluating the same authored coefficients. The underflow limitations of the error transformations remain, and convergence still requires the unchanged original-coordinate feasibility and gap criteria. Reported objective scalars round individually; the internal gap retains their low parts before that rounding.

Every Rust path below is pinned to [Clarabel.rs revision `25540f559592068d0c8a80e46ded1b21760212a1`](https://github.com/oxfordcontrol/Clarabel.rs/tree/25540f559592068d0c8a80e46ded1b21760212a1). The TypeScript versions change language, storage and supported cones while retaining the indicated numerical structure. Shared numerical constants additionally come from `src/solver/implementations/default/settings.rs` at that same revision.

These five files retain `Copyright 2022 University of Oxford Control Group`, `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`, a prominent AutoMovie TypeScript-specialization modification notice, the pinned revision, original Rust paths and the retained license location. The complete upstream [Apache-2.0 license and copyright notice](licenses/clarabel-0.11.1/LICENSE.md) are preserved byte-for-byte: SHA-256 `6e2f382771f8aab58e4868ddd0afe0c2fefe6b54f9681493a9c3d0f32906cfe1`. The inspected pinned source tree contains no separate `NOTICE` file. Existing third-party notices from the historical executable remain preserved as well.

The engine's MIT license continues to cover its separable original code and does not replace the Apache terms for these five adapted files. [Apache section 4](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) requires distribution of the license, prominent modified-file notices and applicable source attribution; any applicable upstream `NOTICE` must also be retained. The engine package's `files` selection includes `src`, `lib` and `vendor/clarabel`. The lifecycle-disabled `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` at 2026-11-06 05:32:56 UTC inspected file selection only. A subsequent normal prepack/build/pack produced an actual local archive with SHA-256 `08e2edd7b16c7adee6024d505e477b4e6f7aa3d6ed30d03633f5fc171692e45d`. Inspection and the corrected token reinspection of that same archive verified all five TypeScript source files, five emitted JavaScript attribution headers, this README and the complete retained Apache license; the extracted public API passed the independent optimum, original-KKT and Farkas-witness smoke checks. That local archive also contains shared Core/construction work in progress, so this distribution check is neither a clean release verdict nor a complete rights audit.

SuiteSparse's LGPL-2.1+ `LDL/Source/ldl.c` was opened later for reference; no C wording, function or processing structure was translated into this patch. The factor's recorded pre-header modification time is 2026-11-06 04:36:11 UTC, and the tool call that first opened the official C source completed with the 04:50:03 UTC observation. This sequence documents what was consulted when; it does not establish an independent origin for the five Rust adaptations or complete a rights audit. Their actual Apache source lineage and distribution obligations are stated above. No LGPL implementation is added as a runtime dependency or copied into the distributed TypeScript.

The previous WASM byte payload, WASI host, Rust bridge, lockfile and executable build inputs have been removed from the engine's shipped paths. Their exact prior source remains in [repository revision 0ed4cd38bd8e4cd115226e42ade4b43587a7f8be](https://github.com/samchon/automovie/tree/0ed4cd38bd8e4cd115226e42ade4b43587a7f8be/packages/engine/vendor/clarabel), and the preserved comparison archives retain the original bytes and SHA-256 records. No active or packaged solver fallback exists. Current workspaces are ordinary call-owned TypeScript arrays; former workspace/host tests now verify actual array and sparse-factor ownership.

## Historical comparisons

The preceding backend used unmodified Clarabel.rs 0.11.1 at the pinned upstream revision stated above. Its interval-to-zero/nonnegative mapping, signed dual reconstruction, cold initialization and full versus reduced status distinctions supplied the compatibility baseline for the TypeScript specialization. The historical infinity sentinel was 1e30 and full feasibility/gap tolerances were 1e-9; the current API retains those boundaries. Optional initial values remain compatibility inputs ignored by the cold solver.

The earlier OSQP comparison is described in [its retained provenance and notices](../quadratic/README.md). Its executable bridge and build inputs are also absent from the current package. Source revisions, licenses and historical comparison findings remain available without shipping an executable alternative.

The shared-method investigation and independently derived nearly parallel constraint family belong to [issue #2498](https://github.com/samchon/automovie/issues/2498); the engine-owned TypeScript replacement belongs to [issue #3091](https://github.com/samchon/automovie/issues/3091). A successful numerical solve does not establish anatomical validity or rendered appearance.
